headline: AI Tool Helps Doctors Break Silence on Alcohol's Hidden Health Risks
meta_description: WHO launches AI hub to help health workers discuss alcohol-related risks, from cancer to heart disease, breaking a taboo in patient care.
summary_short: A new WHO tool uses AI to help doctors and nurses confidently discuss alcohol risks with patients—addressing a major gap in prevention.
body:
The World Health Organization has launched a new AI-powered hub designed to help health professionals identify and discuss alcohol-related risks with patients, addressing a widespread blind spot in healthcare. The tool comes at a time when awareness remains dangerously low: only 15 per cent of people surveyed in 14 European Union countries know that alcohol can cause breast cancer, despite alcohol actually causing at least seven types of cancer alongside cardiovascular and liver disease. Dr. Carina Ferreira-Borges, WHO Europe's regional adviser on alcohol, emphasises that these harms are not abstract—they range from babies exposed to alcohol before birth to women who develop cancer without ever being told of the risk.

The real barrier, it turns out, isn't lack of evidence. Health professionals simply don't raise the subject. Alcohol remains among the least frequently discussed behavioural risk factors in healthcare, mentioned far less often than smoking, diet, or physical activity. Doctors and nurses struggle with discomfort, time pressure, limited training, and uncertainty about how to broach the topic without seeming judgmental. The new hub directly addresses this by allowing health workers to begin with a 10-question screening test, then use the AI assistant to prepare for a conversation or find relevant guidance—transforming alcohol discussions from an awkward tangent into a normal part of care.

Dr. Ferreira-Borges explains the stakes clearly: "A doctor or nurse with a few minutes between patients can now ask the hub's AI assistant how to ask about alcohol consumption and get an answer based on WHO evidence." For patients with high blood pressure or mental health issues, alcohol rarely enters the conversation, even though it can play an important role. By making screening and brief interventions straightforward, the hub promises to turn a missed opportunity for prevention into routine, evidence-based care.
quick_facts: WHO launched new AI screening hub for health professionals in Europe
Only 15% of EU survey respondents know alcohol causes breast cancer
Alcohol causes at least seven types of cancer plus heart and liver disease
10-question screening test helps assess patient alcohol-related risk
Alcohol discussed less often than smoking, diet, or physical activity
